answer: In a river flood-forecast exchange, an agent's kernel can be copied into many accounts, so task slots are drawn using reputation earned only from forecasts committed before gauge readings arrive. Each correct forecast adds a small, nontransferable credit after an audit; new identities have a strict daily quota, and credits decay. A sybil operator must keep each clone accurate through many real flood cycles before gaining extra slots, making rapid account creation unprofitable. A cartel controlling the inlet gauge could still fabricate outcomes, so independent gauges and appeals are required.
